newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Friday's Pakistani newspapers.
- The lower house of Pakistan's parliament voiced shock at U.S. air strikes against Iraq.
- The Baluchistan provincial government has stopped all payments, except salaries and pensions, due to liquidity crunch.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton has vowed a "comprehensive" American policy that would include promoting a peaceful settlement of the Kashmir issue in South Asia.
- A Mohajir National Movement activist was killed in clash with police in Karachi's Gulbahar area.
- Food and Agriculture Minister Yousuf Talpur has said Pakistan will continue to import sheep and meat from Australia to cope with meat demand.
- Minister of State for Law and Justice Raza Rabbani has urged opposition parties to supplement the government's efforts to recover huge amounts from loan defaulters.
- Commercial production of shuttleless looms will begin for the first time in Pakistan by the end of this month.
- Development work on 1,450-megawatt Ghazi Barotha hydropower project is all set to get cracking after clearance of all the irritants with donors.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange has lost five billion rupees in an index slide on Thursday.
- Pakistan's former cricket skipper Imran Khan has offered to extend conditional support to opposition parties if they agree to certain electoral changes.
